title: Names → locations → connections
text: The order of the notes suggests that recognition comes first, then the physical relationships between parts. Teach new vocabulary beside a location and one checked connection so that terms accumulate into a usable model.
next: Try explaining one component without looking, then identify the missing part of the explanation.

title: The notebook returns to earlier questions
text: Later socket pages revisit the early inventory with more precise questions. The narrative should preserve this return, because learning is often refinement rather than a straight replacement of old pages.
next: Add a dated correction and backlink instead of overwriting the earlier observation.

title: A preference for complete systems
text: The recurring requests for every card, socket, cable and test suggest a preference for comprehensive reference and explicit structure. This is a writing preference inferred from the notes, not a personality diagnosis.
next: Use compact bullet points with a clear scope, a source and an explicit boundary.

title: The voice can stay curious and exact
text: Use the learner's voice for the question being pursued and SIFT's voice for limits and connections. Do not put new confident beliefs into the author's mouth. A revised sentence can be cleaner without being more certain.
next: Keep source wording available beside each revision.

title: Recall should test relationships
text: Remembering a label is useful; explaining what it connects to is stronger. A small recall exercise can expose the gap between recognizing a part and understanding its place in a system.
next: Ask: identify it, point to its endpoints, and say which part of that explanation still needs a source.

title: A damaged training unit can teach a false map
text: Broken sideband sockets may make a novice misremember an absent connection as an intentional design. This is plausible from page 40, but its frequency and impact have not been measured.
next: Label the damaged locations on an approved training reference before adding more detail.

title: The missing catalog becomes an outdated catalog
text: The source revises its initial impression of no error reference after finding an SOP presentation. The problem may be retrieval, revision control or scope rather than complete absence.
next: Locate the existing owner and revision before duplicating the catalog.

title: A failure label is not a cause
text: The notebook itself notices the risk of repeating a displayed failure as a diagnosis. A useful entry separates the reported test failure, direct observations, possible explanations and the evidence required for a repair decision.
next: Use those four fields in the next synthetic case note.

title: Time is part of the evidence
text: Present power state and an older event are not interchangeable. Without timestamps, an apparent contradiction may simply describe a changed state.
next: Capture the source and time for each observation, before any approved clearing action.

title: Clearing is a distinct action
text: HMC clearing appears repeatedly, with conflicting syntax and no retention rule. It may be a preparation requirement, but the supplied material cannot establish that or define when evidence has been preserved.
next: Resolve the exact script behavior and applicable retention procedure.

title: A flash is not proof of exclusion
text: A component connection can motivate investigation; it cannot by itself justify flashing or prove a cause eliminated. The page 32 inference should stay visibly hypothetical.
next: Request the supported recovery conditions and the evidence used to judge the result.

title: NvDebug may be an evidence handoff problem
text: The reported delay around some Bianca orders may concern evidence being absent, inaccessible or hard to interpret. Those are different problems and need different remedies.
next: Ask for a de-identified description of a blocked case: what was missing, who needed it, and where it should have lived.

title: One unit appears in several systems
text: The same work is represented by a physical location, ServiceMe, Fusion Eye, the Traveler and tracking sheets. Reconciliation may be more valuable than creating another destination for updates.
next: Map which system owns identity, stage, test result, location and next action.

title: Pass needs a scope
text: The Pass update and subsequent Run-In steps may describe an intermediate success. The notes do not establish when a unit is fully complete.
next: Ask which exact result permits each next transition.

title: Holds need owners
text: Do Not Move, Do Not Touch and Move tags are visible or mentioned, but their release conditions are not. Treating status as permission would hide an important part of the workflow.
next: Record the role that sets and releases each hold and where that authority is recorded.

title: Waiting is worth distinguishing from work
text: Curing, refill, evidence collection and destination decisions may consume elapsed time differently from hands-on work. Their relative contribution is unknown.
next: For a small permitted sample, record the wait category and duration without ranking coworkers.

title: Accessory and scan mistakes may be preventable
text: Repeated mentions of scan arguments, SSD generations and loopbacks suggest opportunities for a configuration-aware preparation reference. The current clues are too uncertain to validate a unit automatically.
next: Obtain one authoritative configuration baseline and test it against a synthetic complete and incomplete record.

title: Handoff quality may reduce repetition
text: If the next team can see what was already checked and what remains uncertain, it may avoid repeating an investigation. The notes suggest this pain but supply no measured saving.
next: Ask a receiver which missing detail most often forces another lookup.

title: Start with retrieval
text: A local searchable field guide offers immediate personal value using already available notes. Retrieval can be useful before any diagnosis is automated.
next: Use this site for a few real learning questions; record missing entries and lookup effort without committing live records.

title: Command Companion precedes Quick Test
text: The alias names are known, but bodies, side effects and output contracts are not. Documenting the existing work preserves credit and provides a testable foundation.
next: Collect sanitized definitions and example outputs for a small scope; keep power changes and clearing distinct.

title: Preflight must explain its finding
text: A future Quick Test should report which reviewed check produced an anomaly, the relevant observed value and what remains unknown. It should not silently turn a heuristic into a failed-part verdict.
next: Prototype with synthetic saved outputs before considering a workplace pilot.

title: Error Muncher needs reviewed actions
text: A tree that retrieves an exact error article is smaller and easier to check than one that diagnoses a unit. Action recommendations should wait for verified scope, prerequisites and outcomes.
next: Begin with exact search and an explicit unknown-code response.

title: Prepare a handoff draft, then review it
text: A local aid could organize the user's observations into stage, result, evidence, interpretation and next question. It should preserve uncertainty and never invent completed checks.
next: Use synthetic input and compare the draft line by line with its source.

title: Avoid an extra board until ownership is clear
text: A shared board can add another stale representation of the same unit. A personal digest may reveal whether the actual need is visibility, timeliness or missing responsibility.
next: Identify one unanswered handoff question and the existing place that should answer it.

title: Do not claim the entire suite as saved time
text: Stage-duration estimates do not tell us how often an early check avoids a suite or whether a test still needs to run. A credible saving needs comparable cases and maintenance cost.
next: Use net effort saved = avoided effort − added checking − upkeep, with inputs marked as estimates until measured.

title: Measure usefulness close to the aid
text: Lookup time, missing-answer count, corrections and repeated voluntary use are closer to a field guide than company-wide unit throughput. They can show whether the aid helps without overclaiming causation.
next: Choose one task type and compare similar attempts, recording exceptions.

title: A graceful unknown is a useful result
text: A reference that says the code mapping is unresolved prevents unsupported certainty. Count clear unknowns separately from incorrect answers when judging the aid.
next: Keep a small set of conflicting and incomplete examples in verification.

title: Keep the smallest useful scope
text: Begin with personal learning and a few repeat questions. Wider adoption adds review and maintenance work that must have an owner.
next: Expand when another person wants a specific benefit; retire a feature if upkeep exceeds repeat value.

title: Stage names, functions and codes need separate fields
text: The FLA/FLC conflict contains at least three independent claims: expansion, operation and code mapping. Settling one does not automatically settle the other two.
next: Ask for the current suite version and one authoritative example for each field.

title: Configuration clues need applicability
text: Color, handle shape, port count and SSD rules may vary by model, revision, training setup or local convention. The notes do not identify those boundaries.
next: Attach each clue to a confirmed model/configuration and source date.

title: The form is a map of records, not proof of sequence
text: The Traveler includes additional rows beyond the initially described route. Their order on paper does not establish mandatory work or which team owns it.
next: Review row ownership, optionality and transition rules with the form owner.

title: What does each component contribute?
text: The final interface notes still ask what each component does for the system. The visual inventory has grown faster than the functional explanation, so that is a strong next learning priority.
next: Choose one component and connect its role, interfaces, observable signals and limits using a trusted source.
